item: One import run takes backups locked with different passphrases, typed once for the common case; a wrong backup passphrase is refused before the checksum pass
key_paths: src/backup/import_queue.py; src/api/backup_v2.py; src/backup/stream_backup.py; src/safety/crypto.py; src/static/app-backup.js; src/static/index.html; tests/test_import_queue_keys.py
summary: The queue carries the run's default keys (the backups' passphrase and, new, the corpus store passphrase of the instance that made them, which /v2/volumes/restore already took and the queue and the Import window could not send) and each item may carry its own pair, which wins for that item alone. Keys are taken out of the item before it is stored, held in memory for the run, scrubbed from every record (ImportQueueManager._secrets) and dropped when it ends. The Import window adds the corpus passphrase field and, when the scan finds more than one backup, a folded per-backup list where an empty field means the one above. read_stream_backup now opens the first chunk of the first volume before verify_volume_set: an intact volume (checksum matches the manifest) that does not open is refused at once; a damaged or missing one gives no verdict, so parity recovery keeps every case it had.
